editorial:
Imagine being a genius math teacher who everyone laughs at, only to find a way to prove them all wrong using a secret formula. You follow a professor who gets kicked out of his job but refuses to give up. He starts using stolen data to build an algorithm that can actually tell you what is going to happen in your life. It feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where the main character is fighting against a world that does not believe in him. The vibe is moody and tense, making you wonder if knowing your future is actually a gift or a total nightmare.

What really works here is how the tension builds as the predictions start coming true. The acting feels natural, and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While it is a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is worth the wait. If you love stories about smart people doing dangerous things, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the professor realizes his algorithm cannot account for human choice and emotion. He discovers that trying to change the future only leads to the very events he tried to avoid. In the final scenes, the twist reveals that his own downfall was predicted from the start. He ends up losing everything, proving that some things are better left as a mystery than solved with math.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mind-bending plots and stories about fate.
